Subject: PoC deployment mode discussion — follow-up and proposed trial plan

Hi Samir & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and a proposed PoC/trial plan so we can get alignment on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and success criteria.

Discovery summary (from today)
- Primary workload: customer support assistant + re-ranking for search.
- Latency sensitivity: mid-to-high for the assistant path (95th pct target) — search rerank can be slightly higher.
- Data residency & compliance: Priya flagged potential requirements for an isolated network and audit logs.
- Throughput expected initially: 20-50 requests/sec during peak.

Recommendation
- Start with a 4-week PoC that validates two deployment modes in parallel: Dedicated capacity for the latency-sensitive assistant flow, and Hosted API for bursty/less-sensitive reranking. If compliance requires it, we can run the Dedicated capacity inside a Private VPC/on-prem equivalent via our Private offering; we should confirm that with your security team during kickoff.

Proposed PoC plan (high level) — see attached Redwood_PoC_plan_v1.pdf
Week 0 (prep): DPA + network/contacts, access, and test data subset
Week 1: Dedicated capacity provisioning + VPC peering (if going private) + sample integration for assistant flow
Week 2: Integration for rerank via Hosted API, baseline latency measurements
Week 3: Load testing and reliability checks, cost estimate based on observed tokens/throughput
Week 4: Review against success criteria and handoff plan

Success criteria (please confirm)
- Assistant flow: 95th-percentile latency < 150ms for 2k token context under target load
- Rerank/embedding calls: average latency < 250ms
- Reliability: <1% error rate under 24h soak at expected peak traffic
- Cost target: within X% of current benchmark (we'll refine once we see baseline usage)

Stakeholders
- Acme: Samir (Engineering lead), Priya (Security), Alicia (Cloud/Infra)
- Redwood: Ben (AE/owner), Jordan (Solutions Engineer), Marissa (Customer Success)

Open items / asks for you
1) Confirm whether Acme needs Private VPC from day 1 or if a Dedicated + VPC peering approach is acceptable.
2) Can Priya share the compliance checklist items we should pre-populate (SOC2, encryption, retention)?
3) Confirm kickoff availability — aiming for week of 1 Mar.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the PoC doclink.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi all — Jordan from solutions engineering here. Quick clarifications to help the decision: 

- Dedicated capacity: provides reserved GPU pools with predictable latency and throughput. We can provision a Dedicated environment in a region close to you and optionally peer it into your VPC for private traffic flows; this is our usual path when teams want the predictability of Dedicated but the network isolation of Private.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): If you require full control over the control plane and an air-gapped setup, Redwood Private is available. That option requires a slightly longer provisioning lead time (typically +2 weeks) and an on-site/partner install if you need air-gap.

- Hosted API: fastest to get started; good for non-sensitive or bursty workloads. Works well in combination with Dedicated for mixed workloads.

Technical asks we can start on this week:
1) Priya: sample network diagram + security checklist (we'll map our peering/network config to yours).
2) Samir: test dataset and an integration endpoint we can hit to validate assistant latency.
3) Acme procurement: any required PO or SOW template — we can attach a DPA for signature while the PoC runs.

I've also added a short runbook to the shared Drive (https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-acme-poc-plan) that covers provisioning steps and expected logs we will provide.

—Jordan
